chapter_theme: Not drinking liquor (கள்ளுண்ணாமை): liquor and lust confuse, destroy truth and understanding and keep people from knowing soul and bond; the sects that drink for power lose it by forgetting themselves. The drink worth taking is the unceasing nectar of Siva's bliss, reached in samadhi, yoga and the union of Siva and Shakti.
structure_note: Verses alternate between condemning liquor and its sectarian users (324, 326 to 330, 332, 335) and describing the true drink, the தேறல் of Siva's bliss (325, 331, 333, 334, 336). The word தேறல், clear toddy, is turned from liquor to bliss.

324.reading: As a cow given rice-wash water seeks no pond yet, craving the slop, wastes its body, so those who drink their fill of liquor have left the right order; the true drink is the clear nectar of Siva's bliss.
324.nuance: கழுநீர் is rice-washing water given to cattle, but can also be the water-lily; the cow image is my best reading of the first two lines. செழுநீர், rich water, describes Siva as the true source of drink.

325.reading: Those who drink the pure honey, the unceasing nectar of Siva's bliss that comes in the samadhi where the mind melts and becomes Siva, do not leave that bliss, whether standing, sitting or lying down.
325.nuance: சுத்த மது, pure honey or wine, keeps the vocabulary of drink for bliss. The last line (நித்தல் இருத்தல் கிடத்தல் கீழ்க் காலே) is obscure; I take it as the postures in which the bliss persists, but கீழ்க்கால் may be a yogic term for the lower breath.

326.reading: Lust and liquor belong to the wretched, and within the sects the great impurity breeds delusion; the mind that goes to the twin feet of the Pure One finds there awareness of the nectar of bliss made of Om.
326.nuance: போமதி may be 'the departing mind' or 'the mind that goes'; ஓமய is read as ஓம்-மய, made of Om, though it could relate to ஓமம், the fire rite. The verse pairs lust and liquor as the chapter does again in 327 and 330.

327.reading: Left-hand worshippers drink liquor and die; the lustful drink the liquor of lust and are confused; those of the fire rite know within the inner light; those of the Name draw near that very day.
327.nuance: வாமத்தோர் are traditionally the followers of the left-hand (Vama) tantra, who use wine in ritual. ஓமத்தோர் may be those of the fire rite or those of Om, and நாமத்தோர் those who repeat the Name; the four groups are ranked.

328.reading: Those who drink liquor do not ponder the inner truth, do not know soul and bond, do not live in the grace the bountiful Lord gave, and do not reach the Siva-yoga of clear true knowledge; they do not know the meaning.
328.nuance: பசு பாசம், soul and bond, are two of the three Siddhanta categories, the third being பதி, the Lord, who appears here as the bountiful நாதன். The charge against liquor is that it blocks Siddhanta knowledge, not only good conduct.

329.reading: Fools in whom the impurity of deluding sects abides, and the great fools who drink deluding liquor, do not discern great maya's delusion or the release from maya; to feel clear inside delusion is itself delusion.
329.nuance: மயக்கு opens every line. The last line can also be read 'if one grows clear of delusion, delusion ends'; I take it as the drunkard's false clarity.

330.reading: Liquor bewilders, dulls and destroys truthfulness; drinkers reach only the pleasure of women and embrace them, and do not go forward into the good knowledge that attains unbroken bliss.
330.nuance: Truthfulness (வாய்மை) is the first casualty named. The two kinds of pleasure, of women and of unbroken bliss, are set side by side through the repeated இயங்கும்.

331.reading: They do not stay in the place where there is neither night nor day and drink, free of distraction, the nectar of bliss; in the joy of the twin feet where there is neither night nor day, night and day and maya are left behind.
331.nuance: The place without night and day is traditionally the state beyond the two breaths, the moon and sun channels, or beyond waking and sleep. The last line (இராப்பகல் மாயை இரண்டிடத் தேனே) is obscure: தேன் may be honey or a first-person ending. The corpus notes a parallel in Kandar Alangaram 74, where staying where there is no night and day is called hard.

332.reading: Sectarians drink liquor seeking power, but the power is destroyed because they forget themselves; real power is to reach Siva-knowledge and join the bliss of truth and knowledge.
332.nuance: சத்தி is both power and the goddess Shakti, whom some sects worship with wine. சத்திய ஞான ஆனந்தம் echoes the formula of being, knowledge and bliss.

333.reading: If the Lord of Shakti gives grace, Shakti's grace follows; if Shakti gives grace, his grace follows; when one holds both Shakti and Siva within, truth and the nature of the eight attainments come.
333.nuance: சத்தன் is the possessor of Shakti, Siva. The mirror-image lines make their grace one. சத்தியம் may be 'truth' or 'it is certain'.

334.reading: Removing the tattvas and delusion, becoming oneself, removing false tapas, entering true enjoyment, taking the world and leaving it: the nectar of Siva's bliss makes the attainment of supreme bliss.
334.nuance: தானாகி, becoming oneself, is traditionally the soul knowing itself apart from the tattvas. மெய்த்த சகமுண்டு விட்டு is obscure; I read சகம் as the world.

335.reading: Yogis who bind the breath taste the nectar of knowledge-bliss from the bright moon and gain the eight attainments; the deluded drink liquor, become fools, fall into infatuation and lose their understanding in intoxication.
335.nuance: கால் is the breath, and ஒண்மதி the moon, traditionally the place in the head from which yogic nectar is said to flow when the breath is held. The two halves set yogic nectar against liquor, both bringing an altered state, one with siddhis and one without understanding.

336.reading: Open the spring where the nectar of the inner water wells, think on the guru's lotus feet, draw near in samadhi; then by the water of the channels the good flows with the eye's stream and is seen along the way of the breath.
336.nuance: நாடிநீர், the water of the channels, கண்ணாறு, the eye's stream, and கால்வழி, the breath's way, are yogic terms whose exact reference I can't fix. நாடி can also be read as 'seeking'. The plain sense is a turn from outer drink to inner nectar under the guru.

links.note: Both find the fault of drinking in self-forgetting: the Kural's drinker pays to buy self-oblivion (மெய்யறியாமை), Tirumular's sectarians lose the power they sought because they forget themselves (தம்மை மறத்தல்).
325 names the nectar of bliss that comes in samadhi; 335 says how, by binding the breath to taste the moon's nectar, and sets it against liquor's loss of understanding.
The Kural simply says do not drink. Tirumular agrees, but keeps the vocabulary of drink: the clear toddy (தேறல்) he commends is Siva's bliss. Abstinence becomes a substitution.
